name: Shoyu Ramen
description: Soy-sauce seasoned brown broth, balanced and savory.
ingredients: Soy tare (1/2 cup soy sauce, 1/4 cup sake, 1/4 cup mirin, 1 Tbsp salt)
instructions: 1. Simmer pork bones, aromatics, and pork belly in water on high for 3 hours, then low for another 3 hours, skimming scum periodically.
2. At 2-hour mark, remove some broth and mix with soy sauce, sake, mirin & salt to create chashu sauce; later turn mixture into tare.
3. After 3 hours, remove pork belly, braise in tare for 2 hours (covered with drop lid), then chill before slicing.
4. Continue cooking broth 3 more hours on low (total 6 hours of simmering).
5. Boil eggs for exactly 7 minutes, then ice-bath them; peel and set aside.
6. Cook noodles per package instructions (about 2–3 minutes), strain.
7. In each bowl, add 1–2 Tbsp shoyu tare, pour in ~1½ cups hot broth, add noodles, top with chashu slices, egg halves, scallions, menma and nori. Serve immediately.

name: Shio Ramen
description: Clear, salty broth—light and delicate.
instructions: 1. In large pot, combine kombu, shiitake, niboshi, bonito flakes in cold water. Steep 4–12 hours (ideally overnight) to make cold brew dashi. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{ index=1}

2. Strain dashi. In saucepan, whisk ½ cup cold dashi, sake, mirin, soy sauce, and salt. Bring to gentle boil, then simmer 5 minutes. Add bonito; if thick shavings, simmer 5 min; thin shavings, steep off heat 10 min. Strain—that's your shio tare. :contentReference[oaicite:2]{ index=2}
3. In pot, heat remaining dashi + chicken or seafood broth over low heat.
4. Boil ramen noodles 2–3 minutes until medium-firm. Drain.
5. Assemble each bowl: pour 1–2 Tbsp shio tare in bottom, add noodles, ladle in hot broth, top with kamaboko, wakame, scallions, and optional chicken/chashu.
6. Serve immediately while hot. :contentReference[oaicite:3]{    index=3}

name: Miso Ramen
description: Hearty miso-flavored ramen, ready in about 30 minutes.
ingredients: ½ cup minced shallots or onion
¼ lb ground pork (or mushrooms for vegetarian)
Chili oil and scallions to garnish
instructions: 1. Heat sesame oil over medium heat; sauté shallots, garlic and ginger ~2 min until fragrant.
2. Add pork (or mushrooms); cook 4–5 min until browned. Stir in doubanjiang, cook 30 sec.
3. Mix miso, soy sauce, and sugar; stir into pot and cook 1 min.
4. Add broth and heat to a simmer, cook 10 min.
5. Meanwhile cook eggs: bring water to rolling boil, add eggs and cook exactly 6½–8 min, then ice-bath.
6. Boil noodles separately ~2–3 min until al dente; drain and set in bowls; heat spinach or corn in final 1 min if using.
7. Pour broth over noodles, top with egg halves, scallions, bamboo shoots, and chili oil as a finishing touch.

name: Tonkotsu Ramen
description: Ultra creamy pork‑bone broth, rich and fatty.
ingredients: Soy tare (½ cup soy sauce, ¼ cup sake, ¼ cup mirin, 1 Tbsp salt)
Chashū pork slices, kikurage mushrooms, scallions, sesame seeds
instructions: 1. Rinse bones, soak cold water 6 hours, drain. Blanche in boiling water and discard scum. Repeat if needed. :contentReference[oaicite:4]{  index=4}
2. Char onion, garlic, ginger (~15 min) until deeply browned. :contentReference[oaicite:5]{      index=5}

3. Combine bones, aromatics, fatback in pot with fresh water. Bring to strong boil then simmer uncovered at medium-high heat for 12–18 hours, skimming scum. Broth becomes opaque and creamy. :contentReference[oaicite:6]{      index=6}
4. Make soy tare in separate pan by simmering soy sauce, sake, mirin, salt until slightly reduced.
5. Boil eggs exactly 7 minutes, then transfer to ice bath; peel.
6. Cook noodles 5–7 min until firm.
7. To serve: add 1–2 Tbsp tare to bowl, add noodles, then ladle hot broth over. Top with chashū, egg halves, scallions, sesame seeds. Serve immediately.

name: Tori Paitan Ramen
description: Creamy chicken‑bone broth, opaque and smooth.
ingredients: Chicken slices or bok choy, soft-boiled egg, scallions
instructions: 1. Clean chicken pieces. In large pot or pressure cooker, add water and chicken bones. Bring to boil, skim scum, simmer uncovered. If pressure cooker, cook 40 min; stovetop about 4 hours with vigorous boil emulsify broth. :contentReference[oaicite:7]{      index=7}
2. Add onion, garlic, ginger, scallions halfway through simmer. Continue until broth cloudy white.
3. Strain broth. Add milk if desired then bring to gentle boil.
4. Boil noodles 2–3 minutes, drain.

5. Assemble each bowl: add shio tare to bowl, pour hot broth, add noodles, top with sliced chicken, bok choy, soft-boiled egg and scallions. Blend broth with immersion blender for frothy texture if desired. :contentReference[oaicite:8]{     index=8}
6. Serve immediately.

name: Tsukemen
description: Cold noodles dipped into hot, concentrated broth.
instructions: 1. Make Tonkotsu broth: boil bones + aromatics 1.5 h, add anchovies & bonito powder, simmer 15 min, strain. ([turn0search0])
2. Marinate pork belly 2 h in soy‑mirin marinade; save leftover marinade for Tsukedare. Slice into 3 mm pieces. ([turn0search0])
3. Make Tsukedare base: sauté garlic & pork mince in sesame oil (~1 min), stir in marinade, miso, sugar, gochujang and sesame seeds. Cook ~1 min. ([turn0search0])
4. Boil noodles per package (~2–3 min), rinse under cold water, drain thoroughly. ([turn0search0])
5. Boil egg 7 min, shock in ice bath, peel. ([turn0search0])
6. Assemble: in dipping-broth bowl mix Tsukedare base and hot broth. Plate noodles with pork slices, egg, green onion. Serve immediately. ([turn0search0])

name: Kaisen Ramen
description: Seafood-based broth with assorted seafood toppings.
ingredients: 500 g mixed seafood (prawns, scallops, clams, mussels)
Chopped spring onions, chili oil, sesame seeds
instructions: 1. Heat oil in pan; sauté scallops ~1 min per side, then prawns until pink (another 2–3 min). Remove and set aside. ([turn0search1])
2. Add ginger; pour in dashi, soy milk, soy sauce, tahini, mirin, miso; simmer gently 5 min until aromatic.
3. Cook noodles 2–3 min, drain.
4. Divide noodles into bowls; pour hot seafood broth over. Top with seafood, scallions, chili oil and sesame seeds. Serve right away.

name: Tokyo‑style Ramen
description: Soy‑dashi chicken broth, medium-bodied with curly noodles.
instructions: 1. In pot, combine chicken broth, dashi, soy sauce, mirin, sake, and salt. Bring to simmer and cook 5–10 min to meld flavors.
2. Separate pot: bring water to boil, cook noodles 2–3 min until al dente. Drain.
3. To serve: divide noodles into bowls, pour hot broth over, top with chashū, nori, sliced scallions. Serve immediately.

name: Sapporo Miso Ramen
description: Hokkaido miso ramen served with corn and butter.
ingredients: 3 Tbsp red or white miso paste
instructions: 1. Bring broth to simmer, remove from heat and whisk in miso paste off-heat (2 min) to preserve flavor.
2. Boil noodles separately 2–3 min until al dente, drain.
3. Heat corn in boiling water for 1 min with noodles or blanch.
4. Serve: place noodles and corn in bowl, ladle miso broth over, top with butter, bean sprouts and chashū slices.

name: Asahikawa Shoyu Ramen
description: Dark, oily soy broth with burnt lard in cold‑weather Hokkaido style.
instructions: 1. Prepare double broth by simmering pork + chicken bones with dried sardines (niboshi) over medium-high heat. Once hot, reduce to simmer for at least 15–20 minutes. Add niboshi early, strain before serving. :contentReference[oaicite:4]{    index=4}
2. While broth simmers, char pork‑fat in pan over low heat for 40 minutes to make burnt lard (mayu). Remove solids, keep oil. :contentReference[oaicite:5]{      index=5}
3. Season broth with soy tare (add around 30 ml per bowl), keep broth warm but do not boil. :contentReference[oaicite:6]{    index=6}
4. Boil noodles 3 minutes (or per package), drain. :contentReference[oaicite:7]{     index=7}
5. Assemble: add burnt lard to each bowl (~1 tsp), pour hot broth, add noodles, top with chashū slices and thinly sliced scallions.
6. Serve immediately.

name: Hakodate Shio Ramen
description: Clear, saline seafood broth typical of Hakodate.
ingredients: Kombu, niboshi or scallops, bonito flakes
instructions: 1. Soak kombu and niboshi in cold water 4–12 h to make dashi; strain. :contentReference[oaicite:8]{      index=8}
2. Simmer broth (pork/chicken + dashi) gently. Season with tare: dissolve salt + mirin, steep bonito for 5 min, strain. :contentReference[oaicite:9]{    index=9}
3. Boil noodles 2–3 min until medium-firm; drain. :contentReference[oaicite:10]{     index=10}
4. Assemble: pour 30 ml tare into warmed bowl, add noodles, ladle hot broth, top with chashū and bamboo shoots, garnish scallions.
5. Serve immediately while broth is clear and hot.

name: Kitakata Ramen
description: Soy‑based broth with thick flat wavy noodles from Kitakata.
ingredients: Pork broth + niboshi (dried sardines) or kombu
Chashū pork, bamboo shoots (menma), scallions, narutomaki
instructions: 1. Combine pork broth with soy sauce, mirin, and dried sardines; bring to gentle boil then simmer 15–20 minutes. Strain. :contentReference[oaicite:11]{      index=11}
2. Boil thick noodles for 5 minutes until chewy; drain. :contentReference[oaicite:12]{   index=12}
3. Slice pre-made chashū; assemble toppings with menma, scallions, narutomaki. :contentReference[oaicite:13]{    index=13}
4. Serve: add sauce/oil to warmed bowl if used, pour in broth, add noodles, top with toppings.
5. Serve hot.

name: Hakata (Kurume) Ramen
description: Kyushu tonkotsu style with thin noodles and rich broth.
ingredients: Chashū pork slices, pickled ginger, sesame seeds
instructions: 1. Rinse bones, soak in cold water for 6 h then drain.
2. Blanche bones twice by boiling and discarding scum (~30 min total). :contentReference[oaicite:2]{     index=2}
3. Char aromatics (onion, garlic, ginger) in skillet ~15 min until deeply browned. :contentReference[oaicite:3]{     index=3}

4. Combine bones, aromatics, water in pot; bring to rolling boil over high heat, skim scum first 20 min. Reduce to simmer for 12 h until creamy opaque broth. :contentReference[oaicite:4]{      index=4}
5. Simmer chashū separately in tare for 2–3 h, chill and slice.
6. Boil noodles ~1–2 min for firm (barikata) texture.
7. Serve: noodles in bowl, pour broth, top with chashū, pickled ginger, sesame seeds.

name: Kagoshima Ramen
description: Kyushu style blending pork-chicken broth, vegetables, dried sardines.
ingredients: Chashū, bean sprouts, mushrooms, scallions, pickled daikon
instructions: 1. Combine tonkotsu broth, chicken broth, water, sardines, sake and mirin; simmer on low 20 min, then strain. :contentReference[oaicite:5]{      index=5}
2. Sear chashū slices ~30 sec/side; scorch scallions ~2 min; sauté mushrooms 5 min, add soy final minute. :contentReference[oaicite:6]{      index=6}
3. Boil noodles ~3–5 min until chewy, drain.
4. Serve: place noodles, pour broth, top with chashū, bean sprouts, mushrooms, scallions, pickled daikon.
cook_time: 20 min broth + 5 min toppings + 5 min noodles

name: Iekei Ramen
description: Yokohama-style pork‑bone broth seasoned heavily with soy, served with thick straight noodles.
instructions: 1. Soak bones overnight, blanch in boiling water and discard scum. :contentReference[oaicite:3]{     index=3}
2. Pressure-cook bones ~1 h, then simmer uncovered ~1–2 h until broth emulsifies. :contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}
3. Prepare tare: blend soy sauces and salt, simmer 1 h until reduced. Chill. :contentReference[oaicite:5]{index=5}
4. Cook noodles ~2 ½ min until firm; drain. :contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}
5. Plate: add tare and chicken oil to bowl (~30 ml tare, 15 ml oil), pour hot broth (~300 ml), add noodles, top with chashū, spinach, nori.

name: Muroran Curry Ramen
description: Hokkaido-style curry-flavored pork-bone ramen with chewy, medium-thick noodles.
ingredients: chashū pork, wakame seaweed, bean sprouts
instructions: 1. Prepare pork-bone broth by simmering bones for several hours. :contentReference[oaicite:7]{index=7}
2. Stir in curry roux (~5 min) until dissolved and slightly thick. :contentReference[oaicite:8]{index=8}
3. Cook noodles ~3–5 min until chewy; drain.
4. Serve: place noodles in bowl, pour curry broth, top with chashū, wakame, bean sprouts.

name: Tantanmen
description: Spicy Japanese sesame‑chili ramen with savory ground pork topping.
instructions: 1. Stir-fry pork with garlic and ginger ~4–5 min until browned. :contentReference[oaicite:9]{index=9}
2. Add sesame paste, chili oil, miso; cook ~1 min.
3. Mix in stock and simmer ~5 min to blend.
4. Cook noodles ~2–4 min until al dente; blanch greens 30–60 sec. :contentReference[oaicite:10]{index=10}
5. Serve: noodles in bowl, broth over, top with pork, greens, scallions.

name: Abura Soba
description: Brothless oily noodles tossed in tare and topped—eaten dry and mixed.
instructions: 1. Boil noodles ~2–3 min; drain and rinse lightly.
2. Toss noodles with tare oil to coat evenly.
3. Top with soft-boiled egg, pork slices, scallions.
4. Mix thoroughly before eating. :contentReference[oaicite:11]{index=11}

name: Mazemen
description: Brothless mixed ramen flavored with soy or sesame sauce, served with toppings.
ingredients: ground pork or tofu mix, egg yolk, scallions
instructions: 1. Boil noodles ~2–3 min, rinse cold and drain. :contentReference[oaicite:12]{index=12}
2. Toss noodles with seasoning sauce until coated.
3. Top with minced pork/tofu, egg yolk, scallions.
4. Mix fully before eating.

name: Tan‑men
description: Light broth ramen topped with stir‑fried vegetables and pork or seafood.
instructions: 1. Simmer broth or dissolve dashi.
2. Stir-fry pork ~3 min, then vegetables ~4 min; season with sake and salt. :contentReference[oaicite:13]{index=13}
3. Boil noodles ~2–3 min; drain.
4. Serve: noodles in bowl, pour broth, top stir‑fried mix.

name: Taiwan Ramen (Nagoya)
description: Spicy ramen style from Nagoya featuring ground pork and garlic chives.
instructions: 1. Stir-fry pork with chili paste ~4–5 min until fragrant.
2. Add broth and simmer ~5 min to infuse spice.
3. Boil noodles ~2–3 min; drain.
4. Serve: pour broth over noodles, top with pork and garlic chives.

name: Vegetarian / Vegan Ramen
description: Broth made from vegetables and kombu, rich in umami without meat.
instructions: 1. Make kombu‑shiitake dashi: soak kombu & shiitake in cold water 30–60 min, then heat to just before boiling and remove kombu. ([turn0search3])
2. In pot, sauté garlic, ginger and scallion whites ~2 min in sesame oil; add miso, soy sauce, mirin, sauté 1 min. Add vegetable broth, simmer ~5 min. ([turn0search3])
3. Boil noodles ~2–3 min until al dente; drain.
4. Assemble bowls: add noodles, ladle broth, top with sliced tofu, mushrooms, greens and scallions.

name: Tonyu Ramen
description: Creamy soy‑milk and dashi broth; vegetarian (may include fish dashi—verify!).
instructions: 1. Prepare dashi individually or use pre-made kombu‑shiitake dashi (steep for ~60 min). ([turn0search3])
2. Sauté garlic, ginger, scallion whites ~2 min in sesame oil; stir-in miso/chili paste ~1 min. Add dashi + mirin, simmer briefly. ([turn0search3],[turn0search15])
3. Add soy milk off‑heat; warm gently 2–3 min (do not boil). Taste and season. ([turn0search3],[turn0search15])
4. Boil noodles ~2–3 min; drain.
5. Serve: noodles in bowl, pour soy‑milk broth, top with greens or tofu.

name: Champon
description: Nagasaki‑style stir‑fry ramen with pork, seafood and vegetables in broth.
instructions: 1. Stir‑fry pork, seafood and vegetables ~5 min in oil until tender.
2. Add broth and noodles to wok/pot; simmer together ~3–5 min until noodles cooked and flavors meld.
3. Serve immediately while hot.

name: Instant Ramen Upgrade
description: Instant noodles upgraded with fresh broth and toppings.
instructions: 1. Boil noodles 2–3 min as packet instructs; drain and discard seasoning packet.
2. Pour fresh broth into pot to re-warm.
3. Serve noodles in bowl, pour broth, top with egg, veggies, meat/tofu.

name: Creamy Miso Tonkotsu
description: Rich fusion broth: tonkotsu pork bone with miso stirred in off‑heat.
instructions: 1. Prepare tonkotsu broth by simmering bones for ~12 h until milky. (as per Hakata style)
2. Remove from heat, whisk in miso off‑heat ~2 min to preserve flavor.
3. Boil noodles ~2–3 min, drain.
4. Serve: noodles in bowl, pour miso broth, top with corn, butter, chashū.

name: Seaweed (Wakame) Ramen
description: Clear shio or shoyu base topped heavily with wakame seaweed.
instructions: 1. Prepare light broth (shio or shoyu tare) by simmering dashi with seasonings briefly.
2. Boil noodles ~2–3 min; drain.
3. Serve: noodles in bowl, pour broth, top generously with wakame and scallions.

name: Tokyo Curry Ramen
description: Soy-based broth with curry powder and toppings.
instructions: 1. Simmer chicken broth and stir in curry seasoning or roux ~5 min until blended.
2. Boil noodles ~2–3 min; drain.
3. Serve: noodles in bowl, pour curry broth, top with pork or vegetables.

name: Yokohama Green Curry Ramen
description: Fusion ramen using Thai green curry broth with chicken and Thai herbs.
instructions: 1. Stir curry paste into chicken or vegetable broth; simmer ~5 min until fragrant.
2. Boil noodles ~2–3 min; drain.
3. Serve: noodles in bowl, pour broth, top with chicken, herbs.

name: Carbonara‑style Ramen
description: Fusion ramen combining creamy Italian-style carbonara sauce with ramen noodles.
ingredients: ¼ to ½ cup grated Parmesan or Pecorino Romano
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: 1. Boil the ramen noodles according to package instructions (usually about 2–4 min). Reserve about ¼–½ cup of cooking water before draining. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}
2. While noodles cook, whisk together egg yolks, grated cheese, and a few cracks of black pepper in a bowl. Set aside. :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}
3. In a skillet over medium heat, render bacon until crisp (~5 min). If any oil is excess, drain leaving about 1 Tbsp. Add garlic for 30 sec if using. :contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}
4. Add drained noodles to skillet, toss briefly to coat in bacon fat. Remove pan from heat. :contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}

5. Immediately add hot noodles (plus reserved cooking water) into egg-and-cheese mixture. Toss vigorously for about 1 min until sauce thickens and coats noodles without scrambling the egg. :contentReference[oaicite:5]{index=5}
6. Return noodles to skillet, stir in bacon, combine gently. Season to taste with salt and black pepper. :contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}
7. Garnish (optional): add corn, fresh basil or scallions on top, then serve immediately while warm. :contentReference[oaicite:7]{index=7}
